flagged_a/repo · 65,143 stars · created 2022-03-15
https://github.com/flagged_a/repo

Unusual star pattern. On 3 of the busiest days, 41% to 90% of the accounts that
starred had no other public stars recorded in GH Archive within 30 days. Bought
or traded stars often look like this, so look closer before you trust the star
count.
Risk: high

Activity
  3,443 forks (53 per 1,000 stars)
  1,414 watchers
      8 issues and pull requests in the last 90 days
  In StarTrust's comparison of 182 organic repos, every one had at least 10
  forks per 1,000 stars. Watchers and issues vary a lot with the kind of repo.
  But most repos flagged for bought stars also had normal numbers here, so
  normal numbers do not prove that the stars are real. Few forks alone also mean
  nothing, because tools such as `composer thanks` star library repos
  automatically.

Busiest days, at least a week apart
  1  2023-11-16  5,082 stars  5,082x normal  unusual spike  41% one-off accounts
  2  2024-01-03  3,337 stars      8x normal                 90% one-off accounts
  3  2023-12-16  1,357 stars      4x normal                 60% one-off accounts
  4  2023-12-09    785 stars      3x normal
  5  2023-11-27    637 stars    637x normal  part of 1

What stands out
- Unusual spike on 2023-11-16: 5,082 stars in one day. A normal day in the four
  weeks before had under 1 star.
- 69% of all stars arrived in 90 days, from 2023-11-16 to 2024-02-13 (about 500
  a day). Before that the repo got about 2 stars a day, and in the last 90 days
  about 2 stars a day.
- Accounts with no other public stars recorded in GH Archive within 30 days: 41%
  on 2023-11-16, 90% on 2024-01-03 and 60% on 2023-12-16. No organic repo in the
  calibration set reached 40%. Most days of repos flagged by research were above
  50%.

Limits
- Anyone can star any repo, so a pattern here says nothing about who arranged
  it.
- GitHub only counts stars that still exist. Stars from deleted accounts are
  missing from the history.
- Account checks use GH Archive, a public third-party record of GitHub events.
  Since June 2025 it has missed a growing share of all stars, and since June
  2026 almost all of them.

Checked <time> using 9 GitHub requests and 3 GH Archive queries,
without a GitHub token. Add --details for the full evidence.
